title: How to Make a TikTok Ad for Your Store | AIVideosUGC
description: How to make a TikTok ad from a product link or one photo, with a script, a presenter, a voice, captions, and a file you can publish to TikTok or Meta.
h1: How to Make a TikTok Ad When You've Never Made One
lead: Here is how to make a TikTok ad: paste the product link or start from one photo, pick one reason to buy, and post a vertical clip with a script, a voice, and captions. Spend only what you can pause.
summary: One reason to buy, a vertical clip that starts with the product in action, then a voice, captions, and a small first campaign.

sections.h2: What you get for a first TikTok ad
paras: A first ad needs one product and one reason someone would buy it. The rest is there so you are not waiting on a creator.

Catch the sound while it is still moving. Jump on a challenge with the product in the action, and come back with a file you can post. "A phone stand that folds flat enough for a jacket pocket" can be shown. "High quality and stylish" cannot.

A voice that carries the line. Generate a voiceover in the language you sell in, or in a second one, including a voice made from a short sample you record. The line should sound like the brand, and you can edit it before the job runs.

A file that is ready to post. Captions, the frame, and a track from the ad music library come with the clip. Publish to TikTok or Meta in one step, or download it and post it yourself. Downloads have no watermark.
sections.alt: Adult woman applies cream from a plain light-peach tube to her cheek at the seaside.

sections.h2: How to go from a product page to a TikTok ad in 3 steps
paras: Three steps. No studio day, and no blank timeline.
Add the product URL. The title, the photos, and the reason to buy come in with the page.
Or upload one photo and one sentence about the action. Leave the price out of that sentence.
A hand unfolds a slim phone stand on a cafe table, in soft daylight. That sentence is enough.
[URL to video](page:url-to-video) is the link path. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) is the photo path.
Pick a presenter from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), make one for the brand, or leave people out.
Anyone on screen is generated. Do not name them as a buyer or a reviewer.
Download the vertical file, or publish it to TikTok. Put the price in the editor and match checkout.
A developer can start the same job through the API from your own shop system.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube over a blank notebook on a bright cafe table.

sections.h2: Reasons to skip the creator wait
paras: The first two seconds have to show the product doing something. A logo card will not hold anyone.

Skip the creator invoice. You do not book an influencer or a crew to get a first opening. A hand snapping a stand open, a drink poured over ice, or a shoe turning to show the sole is a complete scene.
Make another one without waiting. A second hook is another job, not another shoot. Run a batch from the same photo when you want several openings. Each one shows its credit cost first.

Speak to more than one market. The same scene can be captioned and voiced in another language, so a second country does not mean a second production. There is no extra shoot. The credits are the cost of the new file.
sections.alt: Two adult hands spread white cream from a plain peach tube across the back of a hand.

sections.h2: How the TikTok ad gets made
paras: Show the product immediately. If it is still off screen when someone scrolls past, they are gone.
More openings from the same photo. Change the hook, the voice, or the first frame and render again. You are not paying a creator for every revision.

Post while the sound is still moving. A native tall clip can go out for a trend this week. Six seconds fits one motion. Ten fits a short demo. Fifteen fits a simple sequence. Thirty fits a longer one.
No reshoot queue. Test scripts, hooks, voices, and shapes from the photo you already have. The editor is in the product, so you are not hopping to another app for captions and the track.
sections.alt: Adult hands turn one plain peach sunscreen tube for a pre-launch check.

sections.h2: The same product, posted on every placement
paras: Build the tall file first, then the shape each placement actually uses. Do not stretch one download and hope.
TikTok. 9:16, product on screen in the first two seconds. The [TikTok ads](page:plat-tiktok) guide is the size detail.
Instagram Reels. The same tall frame. Do not drop a square file into Reels. [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) covers the feed beside it.
Facebook. Reels stays tall. The feed wants 1:1, and every carousel card should match. See [Facebook](page:plat-facebook).
YouTube Shorts. 9:16 again, with words clear of the bottom and the right edge. [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts) is the placement.
Shopify. The clip can sit on the product page people land on. The offer in the ad and the price at checkout have to match.
Amazon and other listings. Use the same product truth. A video ad and a listing still are different jobs. Sizes for every placement are in [ad sizes by platform](page:guide-ad-sizes-by-platform).
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube beside a notebook on a bright desk.

sections.h2: How shops use a first TikTok ad
paras: These are examples of how a shop would use it, not quotes from a customer.
Example. A candle shop pastes the product URL and gets a tall clip of the lid coming off, then reads it on a phone before spending.
Example. A phone-stand shop picks a presenter from the actor library and never calls that person a buyer.
Example. A drink shop writes the price and the line in the editor, and picks a track from the ad music library.
Example. A pet shop renders the same demo again in a second language for a second market.
Example. A fashion shop publishes the file to TikTok and downloads a copy for Meta.
Example. A supplement shop runs two hooks as two jobs, with the same audience and the same budget, and waits a few days before calling a winner.
Example. A home shop keeps captions in the middle so the buttons on the right do not cover the offer.
Example. A beauty shop starts from a still and one sentence, then checks the shade against the real bottle.
Example. A jewelry shop adds a voiceover in a second language and reads every word before it launches.
Example. A gadget shop asks a developer to start the clip from their listing system through the API when a new product goes up.
One product, one reason, a 9:16 clip that starts with the action, plus a script, a voice, captions, and a licensed track.
Credits are 24, 40, 60, or 120 for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. The cost shows first, a failed job returns the credits, and the download has no watermark. Start with a budget you can pause.

faq.q: Where do I make a TikTok ad if I have never made one?
faq.a: Start here from a product link or one photo. You get a 9:16 clip with a script, a presenter if you want one, a voice, and captions. You still choose the audience and the budget in TikTok.

faq.q: Can the pictures match my brand?
faq.a: Yes. The product photo, your colors, and your line drive the clip. Check the label, the color, and the price against the page you will send people to before you launch.

faq.q: How long does a first TikTok ad take to make?
faq.a: It is one job, not a shoot. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. The cost shows before the job starts. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: How does a product page become the video?
faq.a: Paste the URL. The title, photos, and the reason to buy come in. You pick a script and, if you want, a presenter. Captions, a track, and the tall frame are part of the file. You can edit the line before it runs.

faq.q: What is a TikTok ad maker in this guide?
faq.a: It turns a product URL or a photo into a TikTok-style clip: UGC-style if you want a presenter, or just the product in action. You do not need a shoot to get the first file.

faq.q: Will this beat an ad I filmed myself?
faq.a: That is not a promise. What you gain is more openings to test. Run them together, with the same audience and the same budget, and read the first few days before you spend more.

faq.q: What do I actually get from doing it this way?
faq.a: A file without a studio day, another version without a reshoot, a look that sits in the TikTok feed, captions and a voice, and a way to try a second language. Downloads have no watermark.

faq.q: Can I aim different versions at different people?
faq.a: You can make several scripts, presenters, and tones, then test them. The ad account is still where you pick the audience. Give each test a few days.

faq.q: Can I make the ad look like my brand?
faq.a: Yes. Set the line, the colors, the voice, and the caption style in the editor. The product on screen should still match the product you ship.
